maya: FYI - Cobalt8B-int4 initial bring-up finished. Great unit-cost but we see a consistent quality delta on multi-paragraph explainers and some structured retrieval responses. Need a 1-paragraph cost-vs-quality summary + a short rollout/recommendation for GTN.

drew: Microbench (dev infra): 230 tok/s/GPU steady, p50 115ms, p95 430ms at 1k ctx. Rough unit cost: ~0.29x vs our 13b-int8 baseline (~$19/1M tokens int4 vs $66 baseline).

maya: Eval snapshot (35k mixed harness):
- quick-chat (support): accept-rate -0.4%
- multi-paragraph explainers (600-1k tokens): surrogate-score -3.9, human flags 4.9%
- retrieval-structured (keyed JSON responses from docs): field-miss +4.3% / wrong-source +2.0%

noah: Runtime note: quantization shows small tokenization drift around punctuation that affects JSON fences. KV cache stable for short-turns; long decodes show slightly higher re-generation.

anya: Compact scorecard we can hand to PMs:
```
Model: Cobalt8B-int4
Slices: quick-chat | explainers | retrieval-json
Quality delta vs baseline: -0.4% | -3.9% | -4.3% (field misses)
Latency p95 (1k ctx): 430ms | 620ms (tail) | 480ms
Unit-cost: 0.29x baseline
Product-risk: Low | Medium-High | High
```

drew: Econ bullets (rounded):
- Unit cost multiplier: 0.29x baseline (~71% token savings)
- Example annualized saving: 60k DAU * 850 tok/day * (1 - 0.29) -> ~36.9M tokens/day saved -> ~ $800k/yr at L0 pricing (approx)
- Ops impact: increased human review workload for explainers and structured retrieval until mitigations land.

maya: Product asked: if we route 25% of traffic and retrieval-json is 3% of requests, what's the absolute bump in invalids? Need both per-1k and per-day for GTN.

anya: Calc: extra_invalids_abs = routing_pct * fail_rate * slice_share = 0.25 * 0.043 * 0.03 = 0.0003225 -> 0.03225% absolute increase overall -> ~0.3225 invalids per 1k requests. For 1M req/day that's ~322 extra invalids/day. We'll show per-1k and per-day.

noah: Mitigations to implement ASAP:
- post-output validator for retrieval-json that auto-reroutes invalid payloads to baseline (cheap fix),
- tighten tokenizer-preserve rules around fence tokens (small infra patch),
- kv-pin windows for long-decode hosts to reduce tail re-gen.

maya: Proposed GTN rollout (conservative):
1) Canary 3% live traffic, allowlist slices: quick-chat and FAQ only.
2) Shadow 30% of explainers and 60% of retrieval-json traffic for 72h with prioritized human labels.
3) Keep retrieval-json holdback at 90% until post-processor reduces invalids to <1.5%.
4) Auto-fallback: validation_fail OR rerank_score < 0.7 -> route to baseline.

drew: Ops config snippet (copyable):
```
canary:
  percent: 3
  allowed_slices: [quick-chat, faq]
shadow:
  explainers: {percent:30}
  retrieval-json: {percent:60}
holdback:
  retrieval-json: 90%
fallback_policy:
  validation_fail: true
  rerank_threshold: 0.7
  fallback_model: baseline-13b-int8
monitoring:
  explainer_flag_alert: 2%_1h
  retrieval_invalid_alert: 1.5%_1h
```

maya: One-line recommendation for GTN: "Cobalt8B-int4 reduces per-token cost by ~71% with low short-chat regressions but meaningful regressions on structured retrieval and long explainers; recommend conservative canary + aggressive shadowing and a retrieval-validator holdback until invalids <1.5%."

ops-bot: Canary cluster created: canary-cobalt8b-2026-03-23. Runbook: https://internal.runbooks/redwood/cobalt8b-canary

maya: Can someone make a 1-slide TL;DR (scorecard + rollout + per-1k and per-day math) for PM comms by EOD? I'll attach the eval CSV. :thumbsup:
